validation_runs.measurement_note: The original failure assertion emitted the full native history before the metric-specific assertion, so exact detection latencies were not retained. That reporting defect was corrected before sequence 3.

observation: The isolated replacement queue passed the first exact three-trial run, failed trials two and three on the immediate repeat, and passed a third run after compact metric reporting was added. The correction therefore did not make the frozen five-second detection bound reliable under repeated direct-Activity fanout-128 execution.
inference: A reserved Activity task queue does not reserve Workflow-task capacity inside the single direct-topology parent Workflow. The parent still has to process the 128-item cohort's Workflow event pressure before it can schedule the replacement, while the child topology distributes that pressure across independent Workflow executions. This is an application concurrency-policy inference, not a Temporal guarantee.
falsifier: Repeated direct/fanout-128 trials that always meet the bound after bounding the admitted protected silent-progress cohort would falsify the claim that unbounded single-Workflow event pressure is required to reproduce the miss; a trace showing prompt parent Workflow-task processing during a future miss would falsify the specific scheduling inference.
correction: Retain the isolated replacement control queue, and apply the existing protected admission window to protected and unfaulted silent-progress fanout above eight while leaving unsafe controls at full fanout. Add a failing policy test first, repeat the exact real direct/fanout-128 case across independent invocations, and run a new append-only pilot root.
